claims.text: A short-time high-temperature aging treatment can induce uniformly dispersed coherent nanoprecipitates in a refractory high-entropy alloy that initially has a predominantly single-phase solid-solution microstructure.
A treatment of approximately 900°C for one hour followed by rapid quenching is an example of an aging schedule capable of producing the proposed nanoprecipitates.
The coherent nanoprecipitates act as barriers to dislocation motion.
The nanoprecipitates increase the critical stress required for dislocation motion and thereby produce precipitation strengthening.
The coherent nanoprecipitates serve as sites for dislocation accumulation.
Interactions between nanoprecipitates and dislocations enhance strain-hardening capacity.
Enhanced strain hardening delays the onset of localized plastic instability.
Delaying localized plastic instability improves overall ductility.
The aged alloy should have a significantly higher yield strength than the untreated alloy of the same composition.
The aged alloy should have greater plastic strain or ductility than the untreated alloy.
Aging-induced coherent nanoprecipitation can simultaneously improve yield strength and ductility rather than improving one through a severe sacrifice of the other.
The proposed effect should hold during ambient-temperature mechanical testing in air.

The proposed treatment should be effective for conventionally cast or similarly processed refractory high-entropy alloys that initially have a homogeneous solid-solution microstructure and no intentional precipitation treatment.
Alloys containing extensive pre-existing coarse precipitates may not respond to the aging treatment in the same way.
Alloys processed by routes that already impart nanostructuring may not respond to the aging treatment in the same way.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts higher ductility, but the falsification rule requires only the absence of a severe ductility loss. Thus, unchanged or moderately reduced ductility could satisfy the stated test even though it would not demonstrate the claimed simultaneous improvement.
